courses.title: A Beginner's Guide to Autonomous Robots
courses.description: In this introductory-level course, we'll explore the world of autonomous robots and robotic systems. We'll cover the fundamentals of robotic architecture and talk about the high-level structure of autonomy software. Starting with traditional methods, we'll learn about key components such as sensing, perception, mapping, localization, navigation, and control. The course also examines current trends and future directions in robotics technology, including the application of foundation models. This course is designed for software engineers, robotics enthusiasts, and anyone interested in understanding the basics of autonomous robotic systems.
learning_objectives: Identify the key components and types of autonomous robots
Describe the basic principles of embodied AI in robotics
Recognize the main elements of robotic systems and architecture
List the primary sensors and perception techniques used in robotics
Outline the fundamental concepts of localization and mapping in autonomous navigation
Recall the basic principles of control systems in robotics
Identify current trends and challenges in robotics, including the use of foundation models
courses.target_audience: This course is designed for software engineers, robotics enthusiasts, and anyone interested in understanding the basics of autonomous robotic systems
courses.technical_requirements: No prior knowledge of robotics is required, but a general understanding of software frameworks and programming concepts is beneficial
courses.notes: Entry point for robotics learning - general interest level, no hands-on component

courses.title: An Introduction to NVIDIA Cosmos for Physical AI
courses.description: In this introductory, hands-on course, learners will explore NVIDIA Cosmos™, a platform of generative world foundation models (WFM), advanced tokenizers, guardrails, and an accelerated data processing and curation pipeline built to accelerate the development of physical AI. This course was originally delivered at GTC in 2025.
learning_objectives: Learn how NVIDIA Omniverse and Cosmos work together to generate physics-based, photorealistic data for training physical AI models
Learn about different types of Cosmos models, including text-to-world and video-to-world generation models
Review video preprocessing, data curation, fine-tuning and guardrails
courses.target_audience: Developers and AI practitioners working with physical AI, generative AI, and world foundation models. Most applicable to those developing AI models for robotics and autonomous systems
courses.technical_requirements: An understanding of AI model training, fine-tuning, and deep learning frameworks; Experience with Python programming; Basic experience with 3D software and workflows
courses.notes: Introduction to Cosmos platform - hands-on course, originally delivered at GTC 2025

courses.title: Getting Started: Simulating Your First Robot in Isaac Sim
courses.description: In Getting Started: Simulating Your First Robot in Isaac Sim, we will begin a comprehensive learning path to begin robotics simulation using Isaac Sim. This beginner-friendly course guides you through building a simple robot by assembling key components such as the chassis, wheels, and joints. You'll then apply physics properties to simulate realistic interactions between the robot and its environment. As you progress, you'll design control mechanisms using ROS 2 and OmniGraph to enable dynamic movement of the robot. You'll integrate advanced sensors like RGB and 2D Lidar to enhance the robot's environmental awareness. Next, you'll transmit sensor data from Isaac Sim to ROS 2 for real-time visualization and analysis in RViz. Finally, you'll learn to diagnose and troubleshoot common issues related to simulation, control, and data streaming to ensure smooth operation of the robot.
learning_objectives: Assemble a simple robot model in Isaac Sim using basic prims as key components such as the chassis, wheels, and joints
Apply physics to simulate realistic interactions between the robot and its environment
Design control mechanisms using ROS 2 and OmniGraph to enable dynamic movement of the robot
Integrate advanced sensors like RGB and 2D lidar to enhance the robot's environmental awareness
Transmit sensor data from Isaac Sim to ROS 2 for real-time visualization and analysis in RViz
courses.target_audience: Beginners to robotics simulation looking to create dynamic simulations and build foundation for future robotics projects
courses.technical_requirements: Basic Python knowledge and familiarity with robotics concepts. A Linux machine meeting Isaac Sim's system requirements is necessary for this course and for properly running simulations
courses.notes: First course in Isaac Sim 5-course learning path - essential entry point

courses.title: Ingesting Robot Assets and Simulating Your Robot in Isaac Sim
courses.description: In Ingesting Robot Assets and Simulating Your Robot in Isaac Sim, we will dive into the process of importing and simulating robots in Isaac Sim. This course builds upon the foundational concepts covered in the first course, which focused on building a basic robot using primitives and setting up physics. Here, we will explore how to import robot assets using the URDF (Unified Robot Description Format) importer. We will then set up control interfaces, including differential controllers and keyboard control, and examine how to add sensors to the robot. The course will end with an introduction to the Isaac Sim robotic assets, providing a hands-on experience with importing and simulating more complex robot models.
learning_objectives: Analyze the structure and components of a URDF file to identify key elements such as joints and links
Apply the URDF importer in Isaac Sim to successfully import and simulate a robot model
Design a control system for a robot using differential controllers and keyboard control interfaces
Evaluate the physics behavior of a simulated robot to identify and resolve issues such as excessive velocity
Create a simulated environment in Isaac Sim that includes a robot model with appropriate physics and control settings
courses.target_audience: Developers who have completed the first Isaac Sim course and want to work with more complex robot models and URDF files
courses.technical_requirements: This is the second course in the Getting Started With Isaac Sim learning path. Please complete Getting Started: Simulating Your First Robot in Isaac Sim before beginning this course. Basic Python knowledge and familiarity with robotics concepts. A Linux machine meeting Isaac Sim's system requirements is necessary for this course and for properly running simulations
courses.notes: Second step in Isaac Sim 5-course learning path

courses.title: Synthetic Data Generation for Perception Model Training in Isaac Sim
courses.description: In this course, you will learn how to train and deploy a perception model using synthetic data generation (SDG) for dynamic robotic tasks. You will analyze the role of perception models, use simulation for SDG, apply domain randomization techniques, and evaluate the effectiveness of a trained model. Through hands-on exercises, you will generate synthetic data, learn how to train a custom AI perception model, and integrate it into a robotic workflow. This course is designed for students familiar with robotics and Isaac Sim, as well as users interested in applying SDG to various robotic disciplines.
learning_objectives: Analyze the role of perception models in dynamic robotic tasks
Apply domain randomization with Replicator to generate synthetic data
Evaluate the effectiveness of a trained AI perception model
Use a workflow for training and deploying a perception model using SDG
courses.target_audience: Students familiar with robotics and Isaac Sim, as well as users interested in applying synthetic data generation to various robotic disciplines
courses.technical_requirements: This is the third course in the Getting Started With Isaac Sim learning path. Please complete Ingesting Robot Assets and Simulating Your Robot in Isaac Sim before beginning this course. Basic Python knowledge and familiarity with robotics concepts. A Linux machine meeting Isaac Sim's system requirements is necessary for this course and for properly running simulations
courses.notes: Third step in Isaac Sim 5-course learning path

courses.title: Developing Robots with Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) in Isaac Sim
courses.description: In this course, you will learn the fundamentals of Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) and how to apply it in robotics development using NVIDIA Isaac Sim and ROS 2. Through a series of modules, you will explore the concept of SIL, its benefits, and how to integrate it with ROS 2 packages for simulation-based testing. You will also gain hands-on experience with visual programming using OmniGraph and testing an image segmentation application in simulated environments. This course is designed for students who are familiar with Isaac Sim and ROS development. It is an introductory-level course, providing a comprehensive introduction to SIL and its application in robotics development.
learning_objectives: Identify key characteristics and challenges of intelligent robots in dynamic environments
Understand Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) and its importance in robotics development
Use OmniGraph to control a robot in Isaac Sim with ROS 2
Demonstrate image segmentation using ROS 2 on pre-recorded data
Design and execute a SIL test for image segmentation using Isaac Sim and ROS 2
courses.target_audience: Students familiar with Isaac Sim and ROS development looking to learn simulation-based testing methodologies
courses.technical_requirements: This is the fourth course in the Getting Started With Isaac Sim learning path. Please complete Synthetic Data Generation for Perception Model Training in Isaac Sim before beginning this course. Basic Python knowledge and familiarity with robotics concepts. A Linux machine meeting Isaac Sim's system requirements is necessary for this course and for properly running simulations
courses.notes: Fourth step in Isaac Sim 5-course learning path - focuses on SIL testing methodology

courses.title: Leveraging ROS 2 and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) in Isaac Sim
courses.description: In this course, you will learn how to transition robotics applications from simulation to real-world deployment using ROS 2, Isaac Sim, and NVIDIA Jetson. Starting with a software-in-the-loop (SIL) application, you will test it using hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) techniques and deploy it on a Jetson. The course covers setting up Jetson hardware, running image segmentation tasks, and validating results in both simulated and real-world environments. Designed for learners with some familiarity with Isaac Sim or robotics, this course is accessible to beginners and valuable for experienced users. While the Nova Carter AMR is used as an example, the skills and concepts taught are applicable across various robotic systems.
learning_objectives: Describe hardware-in-the-loop systems
Execute image segmentation tasks
Apply Isaac ROS in real-world scenarios
Analyze results from simulation to real-world tests
Install and configure NVIDIA Jetson
courses.target_audience: Learners with some familiarity with Isaac Sim or robotics, accessible to beginners and valuable for experienced users looking to deploy on real hardware
courses.technical_requirements: This is the fifth course in the Getting Started With Isaac Sim learning path. Please complete Developing Robots with Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) In Isaac Sim before beginning this course. Basic Python knowledge and familiarity with robotics concepts. A Linux machine meeting Isaac Sim's system requirements is necessary for this course and for properly running simulations
courses.notes: Fifth and final step in Isaac Sim 5-course learning path - bridges simulation to real hardware deployment

courses.title: Software-in-the-loop Testing for Robots with OpenUSD, Isaac SIM, and ROS
courses.description: This lab focuses on software-in-the-loop for testing and validating AI-driven robots in a digital twin environment. Participants will learn to assemble a virtual environment using OpenUSD and NVIDIA Isaac Sim. You'll add virtual robots to the scene and simulate and validate their basic movements with ROS (Robot Operating System) commands. The lab will emphasize data aggregation, environment creation, and initial robot simulation. By the end of this lab, you'll be able to create and leverage a digital twin environment to simulate basic robot movements within it using ROS. This lab is designed for developers interested in digital twin technology and robotics simulation in industrial settings. This course was originally delivered at GTC in 2025.
learning_objectives: Learn how to launch Isaac Sim and integrate it with ROS 2 for seamless communication between your simulation and ROS nodes
Develop ROS-compatible graphs for sensors like Lidar, control mechanisms like Twist subscribers, and odometry publishers
Build environment maps that robots can use for navigation and obstacle avoidance
Use tools like MoveIt2 for manipulation tasks and Nav2 for autonomous navigation
Combine navigation and manipulation skills to complete a simulated task involving multiple robots
courses.target_audience: Developers interested in digital twin technology and robotics simulation in industrial settings
courses.technical_requirements: Experience with OpenUSD, NVIDIA Omniverse and 3D CAD software. Experience in Python. Basic knowledge of NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac ROS
courses.notes: Alternative/parallel path after SIL basics - focuses on digital twin and advanced ROS integration, originally from GTC 2025

courses.title: Develop, Simulate, and Deploy Robot Intelligence with Scaled Foundations
courses.description: Robots hold massive potential to automate and scale difficult and repetitive tasks across industries and in our lives. Programming robots to conduct these tasks safely has historically been challenging, costly, and specialized. Robotics simulation enables developers to virtually train, test and validate robots in physics-based digital representations of the real world. In this lab, we'll take you through the end-to-end robotics development process using Scaled Foundations' GRID platform powered by NVIDIA Isaac Sim. Starting with a fully functional robot simulation instance with a robot, sensor, AI model, and environment, you'll create an end-to-end, functional robot solution to perform a task and combine your robot solution with several of the latest robot AI models. Finally, you'll see how you can take your solution from GRID and deploy on a real robot.
learning_objectives: Initiate a fully functional robot simulation instance with robot, sensor, AI model, and environment
Create an end to end, functional robot solution to perform a task
Combine your robot solution with several of the latest robot AI models, run this AI solution through simulation, and improve performance
Take a solution from GRID and see it deployed on a real robot
courses.target_audience: Developers interested in end-to-end robotics development from simulation to real-world deployment
courses.technical_requirements: Basic knowledge of NVIDIA Isaac Sim, robotics fundamentals, and Python
courses.notes: End-to-end robotics development using Scaled Foundations GRID platform - covers simulation to real robot deployment

courses.title: Generating High-Quality Motion Data for Robotics with MobilityGen
courses.description: This tutorial introduces MobilityGen, a new toolset built on NVIDIA Isaac Sim for generating high-fidelity motion data to train and evaluate mobile robots. Learn how MobilityGen supports various robot types and data collection methods, including teleoperation and procedural generation, and how it can record and replay robot trajectories with rich ground truth data.
learning_objectives: Understand the importance of high-quality motion data in robotics
Learn the key components and features of MobilityGen
Set up and use MobilityGen with NVIDIA Isaac Sim
Record motion data using teleoperation and procedural generation methods
Replay trajectories and render sensor data
Visualize and analyze the collected data using Gradio
courses.target_audience: Developers interested in robot mobility research and development
courses.technical_requirements: Isaac Sim 4.5 and corresponding technical specifications, basic understanding of robotics and simulations
courses.notes: Featured course from your example - fully completed as sample

courses.title: An Introduction to AI-Based Robot Development With Isaac ROS
courses.description: The beginner-friendly course provides a foundational understanding of NVIDIA Isaac ROS, a robotics framework built on the open-source Robot Operating System (ROS). The course aims to introduce developers new to robotics to Isaac ROS, explaining what it is, its purpose, and how it leverages NVIDIA acceleration to enable AI-based robots. It covers the importance of ROS and how Isaac ROS packages are designed to work seamlessly with ROS 2.
learning_objectives: Explain the purpose of Isaac and how it enables others in the field of robotics
Describe Isaac ROS and its components
Understand the role of ROS 2 and NITROS within the Isaac framework
Utilize developer resources to accelerate your development with Isaac ROS
courses.target_audience: Developers new to robotics who want to understand Isaac ROS and how it enables AI-based robot development
courses.technical_requirements: No prerequisites are required to take this course
courses.notes: Quick intro to Isaac ROS - general interest level, no hands-on component

courses.title: Accelerating ROS 2 with NVIDIA GPU-Powered Libraries and AI Models
courses.description: Learn how to accelerate ROS 2 workloads using NVIDIA's latest GPU-powered libraries for AI and robotics. This hands-on lab will explore how to leverage Generative AI and GPU-accelerated ROS 2 packages to enhance robotic workloads in real-time. Participants will gain experience with optimizing ROS 2 packages for GPU acceleration, including techniques for improving performance and reducing latency in AI perception, navigation, and more. The session will also demonstrate NVIDIA Isaac's powerful AI and simulation tools, designed for seamless integration with ROS 2. This course was originally delivered at GTC in 2025.
learning_objectives: Learn to utilize NVIDIA's GPU-powered libraries to accelerate ROS 2 workloads, enhancing AI and robotics performance in real-time applications
Gain experience in leveraging Generative AI and GPU-accelerated ROS 2 packages to optimize robotic workloads, focusing on AI perception and navigation
Understand techniques for improving performance and reducing latency in ROS 2 packages through GPU acceleration
Explore the integration of NVIDIA Isaac's AI and simulation tools with ROS 2 for seamless enhancement of robotic applications
courses.target_audience: Experienced robotics developers and ROS 2 practitioners looking to optimize performance using GPU acceleration and AI models
courses.technical_requirements: Experience with OpenUSD, NVIDIA Omniverse and 3D CAD software. Experience in Python. Basic knowledge of NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac ROS
courses.notes: Advanced paid course for ROS 2 optimization - hands-on lab, originally delivered at GTC 2025

courses.title: An Introduction to Robot Learning and Isaac Lab
courses.description: Robot learning is revolutionizing how machines interact with their environments, but have you ever wondered what robot learning really is? This overview will explore the fundamentals of robot learning and introduce NVIDIA's Isaac Lab, a powerful tool for developing robotic applications. By the end, you will understand the basics of robot learning, Isaac Lab's key features, and how this framework fits into the broader robotics landscape. We'll explore available robots and environments within Isaac Lab, as well as peek at the product roadmap.
learning_objectives: Explore the fundamentals of robot learning and the algorithms that drive it
Discover how Isaac Lab fits into the Isaac Sim ecosystem and its core functionalities
Identify potential applications and customer bases for Isaac Lab
Dive into the processes for designing environments, from asset import to policy deployment
Understand workflows for transitioning simulations to real-world applications
courses.target_audience: Anyone interested in robot learning - no prior robotics knowledge required, general understanding of software frameworks helpful
courses.technical_requirements: No prior knowledge of robotics is required, but a general understanding of software frameworks and programming concepts is beneficial
courses.notes: First course in Isaac Lab learning path - general overview suitable for beginners, no robotics experience required

courses.title: Transferring Robot Learning Policies from Simulation to Reality
courses.description: Welcome to our course on Transferring Robot Learning Policies From Simulation to Reality, which we often refer to as sim-to-real. While this course won't focus specifically on Isaac Lab, the principles we'll cover are important to understand before you start developing robot learning policies in Isaac Lab. Our goal in this course is to teach you about sim-to-real, including best practices and pitfalls to avoid.
learning_objectives: Understand the challenges of reinforcement learning in robotics
Explain the concept of the 'reality gap' and its characteristics
Describe various techniques for bridging the reality gap
Evaluate strategies for leveraging privileged information in robot learning
Implement best practices for successful sim-to-real transfer in robotics applications
courses.target_audience: Anyone interested in understanding how simulated robot learning transfers to real-world applications - no hands-on component
courses.technical_requirements: This course does not have a hands-on component. No prerequisites are required to take this course
courses.notes: Theory course bridging simulation and real robots - focuses on sim-to-real principles, not Isaac Lab specifics. No hands-on component

courses.title: Train Your First Robot in Isaac Lab
courses.description: Step into the world of intelligent robotics with Train Your First Robot with Isaac Lab—a hands-on course designed to launch your journey into reinforcement learning and physical AI. Using NVIDIA's Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab, you'll discover how to teach robots new skills through reinforcement learning and simulation—no prior robotics experience required. You'll gain practical experience building, training, and evaluating robot behaviors in a virtual environment, setting the stage for real-world applications and the future of adaptable, autonomous machines.
learning_objectives: Learn about Physical AI, and how it's changing the ways robots learn and perform tasks
Describe the core principles of reinforcement learning (RL) and their relevance to robotics using Isaac Lab and Isaac Sim
Identify and configure the essential components of an RL task within Isaac Lab
Apply an Isaac Lab workflow to train, evaluate, and refine a robot control policy in simulation, using the cartpole
Analyze training results of learned policies
courses.target_audience: Anyone interested in robot learning - no prior robotics experience required, hands-on learners ready to build their first RL robot
courses.technical_requirements: Basic familiarity with Python, the command line, and robotics concepts
courses.notes: First hands-on training course - uses cartpole example to teach RL fundamentals. Duration updated to 3 hours per website

courses.title: Train Your Second Robot in Isaac Lab
courses.description: In this course we'll go deeper into Isaac Lab, with a hands-on activity to configure and train a UR10 robot to perform a task you'll design. In our first training course you were introduced to the task workflow and the robot you were training was completely configured. Now it's time for you to configure your own robot, design your own training task, develop reward functions, and configure training hyperparameters. By the end of this course you will be able to configure new robots in Isaac Lab and create and train reinforcement learning tasks.
learning_objectives: Configure a custom robot in Isaac Lab to prepare it for training
Design a reinforcement learning task tailored to specific objectives
Develop reward functions to guide robot learning and task performance
Train a robot to perform a task using reinforcement learning techniques
Evaluate and compare the performance of different trained policies
courses.target_audience: This course is designed for developers, roboticists, and AI practitioners interested in reinforcement learning and robot training in simulation. It is most applicable to those working with physical AI and robotics applications
courses.technical_requirements: Basic Python programming skills, familiarity with command line interfaces, and an understanding of fundamental robotics concepts are recommended
courses.notes: Second hands-on training course - more advanced than 003, focuses on custom robot configuration and task design with UR10

courses.title: Getting Started with AI on Jetson Nano
courses.description: The power of AI is now in the hands of makers, self-taught developers, and embedded technology enthusiasts everywhere with the NVIDIA Jetson developer kits. This easy-to-use, powerful computer lets you run multiple neural networks in parallel for applications like image classification, object detection, segmentation, and speech processing. In this course, you'll use Jupyter iPython notebooks on your own Jetson to build a deep learning classification project with computer vision models. You'll learn how to set up your NVIDIA Jetson Nano and camera, collect and annotate image data, train neural networks on your data to create your own models, and run inference on the Jetson Nano with the models you create.
learning_objectives: Set up your NVIDIA Jetson Nano and camera
Collect image data for classification models
Annotate image data for regression models
Train a neural network on your data to create your own models
Run inference on the NVIDIA Jetson Nano with the models you create
Create deep learning classification and regression models with Jetson Nano
courses.target_audience: Makers, self-taught developers, and embedded technology enthusiasts interested in running AI on edge devices
courses.technical_requirements: Supported Jetson Developer Kit (Orin Nano, AGX Orin, Jetson Nano, or 2GB Nano). High-performance microSD card (32-64GB). 5V 4A power supply for Nano. Logitech C270 USB Webcam or similar. Computer with internet connection and ability to flash microSD card. Basic familiarity with Python (helpful, not required)
courses.notes: Self-paced 8-hour course requiring Jetson hardware - covers setup, image classification, and regression projects

courses.title: Getting Started with AI on Jetson Nano
courses.description: The power of AI is now in the hands of makers, self-taught developers, and embedded technology enthusiasts everywhere with the NVIDIA Jetson developer kits. This easy-to-use, powerful computer lets you run multiple neural networks in parallel for applications like image classification, object detection, segmentation, and speech processing. In this instructor-led workshop, you'll use Jupyter iPython notebooks on your own Jetson to build a deep learning classification project with computer vision models. This interactive format provides live instructor guidance and support as you work through hands-on projects.
learning_objectives: Set up your NVIDIA Jetson Nano and camera
Collect image data for classification models
Annotate image data for regression models
Train a neural network on your data to create your own models
Run inference on the NVIDIA Jetson Nano with the models you create
Create deep learning classification and regression models with Jetson Nano
courses.target_audience: Makers, self-taught developers, and embedded technology enthusiasts who prefer live instructor guidance while learning to run AI on edge devices
courses.technical_requirements: Supported Jetson Developer Kit (Orin Nano, AGX Orin, Jetson Nano, or 2GB Nano). High-performance microSD card (32-64GB). 5V 4A power supply for Nano. Logitech C270 USB Webcam or similar. Computer with internet connection and ability to flash microSD card. Basic familiarity with Python (helpful, not required)
courses.notes: Instructor-led 6-hour workshop version - same content as self-paced but with live instructor support and interactive sessions
